events.outcome: Conditional on the usual relative fibre D=Fib(RΓ(B_G,N)→RΓ(X,N)) and an abelian G-module N in degree zero. In the internal G-action model, the H^0 restriction is the forgetful map from equivariant global sections to underlying global sections, hence injective because the forgetful functor is faithful. Both derived-section complexes have no negative cohomology. The long exact sequence gives H^i(D)=0 for i<0 and H^0(D)=ker(H^0(B_G,N)→H^0(X,N))=0. For the cohomological shift, H^i(D[1])=H^{i+1}(D); therefore τ_{≤2}(D[1]) has possible cohomology in degrees 0,1,2, corresponding to H^1,H^2,H^3 of D. This verifies the stated lower bound and the displayed shift/truncation range under the fibre interpretation. It does not prove the claimed classification by Gr-champs or strict Picard 2-categories.

Conditional internal-action calculation: let B_G denote G-objects over a base topos X and P=G with left regular action. For a G-equivariant p:S→G, let T be its fibre over the identity. The map G×T→S, (g,t)↦g·t, has inverse s↦(p(s),p(s)^{-1}·s). Equivariance ensures the second component lies over the identity, and both composites are identities; equivariant maps over G correspond to maps between those fibres. Thus (B_G)_{/P} is equivalent to X in this action model. For the trivial group e, B_e is likewise equivalent to X. This checks the proposed slice example, not the source identity of the tiny e/c subscript or the 2-gerbe classification.
